mainTopic: ברכות over grain foods and bread crumbs, and which unusual breads need חלה
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה reports the argument between רבן גמליאל and the חכמים about the ברכה after grain, the seven species, and rice. Another line in the same תוספתא shows it cannot follow רבן גמליאל, so the גמרא assigns it to the רבנן and corrects its rice line: after rice, there is no ברכה מעין שלש. Next, רבא rules on ריהטא, a flour-and-honey dish. He first splits by recipe, then retracts and says both get בורא מיני מזונות, based on רב and שמואל's rule about the five grains. רב יוסף says bread pieces in a cooked dish get המוציא only if they are a כזית, and he brings a proof from מנחות. אביי challenges the proof, and the answers go back and forth. The final ruling, from רב ששת and רבא, is that even smaller crumbs get המוציא as long as they still look like bread. The amud ends with unusual baked items, טרוקנין and טריתא, and whether they need חלה. A contradiction about bread made for כותח is resolved with רבי יהודה's rule that the way it is made shows its purpose, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Seven species or unbaked grain: three blessings vs. one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. For food from the שבעת המינים that is not grain, or grain not made into bread, רבן גמליאל requires three ברכות after eating. The חכמים require one.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Anything from the seven species) that is not a grain, or is a grain but was not made into bread: רבן גמליאל says three blessings, and the חכמים say one blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of quoting a ברייתא, where רבי יהודה reports what רבן גמליאל held. This part covers foods like dates or cooked grain that is not bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל treats these foods like real bread and requires full ברכת המזון. The חכמים say they only need one ברכה מעין שלש. This sets up the next line, which goes one level lower, to rice.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven special species of ארץ ישראל
A species of grain (wheat, barley, etc.)
Three blessings, meaning full ברכת המזון
One blessing, the short ברכה מעין שלש

phrases.english: and it is not a species of grain,
phrases.notes: Still the ברייתא's case: something from the seven species that isn't grain, like dates.

phrases.english: or it is a species of grain
but one did not make it into bread —
Rabban Gamliel says: three blessings,
and the Sages say: one blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא מִין דָּגָן הוּא, אוֹ מִין דָּגָן וְלֹא עֲשָׂאוֹ פַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun on the previous amud
steps.raayaObject: Identifying whose view the תוספתא about rice follows
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יהודה quoting רבן גמליאל

steps.title: Rice and millet bread: one blessing vs. nothing
steps.stepSummary: For rice or millet bread, רבן גמליאל requires a ברכה אחת מעין שלש after eating, while the חכמים say no such ברכה is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything that is neither from the seven species nor a grain, like rice bread or millet bread: רבן גמליאל says one blessing that summarizes the three, and the חכמים say nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reaches rice. In רבי יהודה's report, רבן גמליאל gives rice a ברכה מעין שלש. That matches the תוספתא, so the תוספתא seems to follow רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבן גמליאל is strict at every level, he even gives rice a ברכה מעין שלש. The חכמים give rice no ברכה מעין שלש at all. This is the key line the גמרא uses to assign the תוספתא to רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rice
Millet
Summarizing the three blessings (על המחיה)
Nothing at all

steps.confusionAlert: "ולא כלום" means no ברכה מעין שלש and no ברכת המזון. One explanation is that one still says בורא נפשות.

phrases.english: Anything that is neither from the seven species
nor a species of grain,
such as rice bread and millet bread —
Rabban Gamliel says
one blessing abridged from the three,
and the Sages say: nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא מִשִּׁבְעַת הַמִּינִין וְלֹא מִין דָּגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא and supplies the line that matches the תוספתא
steps.raayaObject: The תוספתא's ruling of ברכה מעין שלש after rice
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן גמליאל's opinion as reported by רבי יהודה

steps.title: Challenge: look at another line in the same תוספתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions assigning the תוספתא to רבן גמליאל. It cites an earlier clause: bread whose pieces are no longer intact gets מזונות before and a ברכה מעין שלש after.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain it, like רבן גמליאל? Read the end of the first section: if the pieces are not intact, at the start one says בורא מיני מזונות, and at the end one says one blessing summarizing the three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It quotes another line from the same תוספתא that will be hard to fit with רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real wheat bread that has crumbled into small bits still gets only a ברכה מעין שלש afterward, per this clause. The next step will show why רבן גמליאל could not have said this.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you establish it? (whose view)
The end of the first section
Intact slices or pieces of bread
The blessing before eating grain foods

phrases.english: How did you establish it? According to Rabban Gamliel?
Say the latter clause of the first section:
if the pieces are not intact —
at the start one blesses over it: 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment,'
and at the end one blesses over it
one blessing abridged from the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקִימְתָּא — כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל? אֵימָא סֵיפָא דְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution reached in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the תוספתא to רבן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another clause in the same תוספתא is too lenient to be רבן גמליאל's view

steps.title: רבן גמליאל would never be that lenient
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל requires full ברכת המזון even for dates and pounded wheat. So he would surely require it for actual bread pieces. The crumbled-bread clause cannot be his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? If רבן גמליאל: now, over dates and pounded wheat רבן גמליאל said three blessings. Is it even a question for bread whose pieces are not intact?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its attack with a קל וחומר. If רבן גמליאל demands three ברכות for lesser foods, he would certainly demand them for real bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crumbled bread is still real bread, which is more important than dates or דייסא. Giving it only a ברכה מעין שלש makes no sense for רבן גמליאל. So this clause, and the whole תוספתא, seems not to be his.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is it?
Dates
Pounded wheat porridge
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.english: Whose is it? If Rabban Gamliel,
now, if over dates and pounded wheat
Rabban Gamliel said three blessings,
when the pieces are not intact, is it even a question?!
phrases.notes: He's asking this rhetorically; of course he would need three blessings then.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי: אִי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הַשְׁתָּא אַכּוֹתָבוֹת וְאַדַּיְיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: Attributing the crumbled-bread clause to רבן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: three ברכות for dates and דייסא, so surely for bread

steps.title: So the תוספתא must be the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Since the clause cannot be רבן גמליאל, the גמרא concludes the תוספתא follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious: the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question "whose view is it?" It says the תוספתא is the רבנן. This answer will immediately create a new problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן give a ברכה מעין שלש for grain that is not proper bread, so the crumbled-bread clause fits them well. But the rice line still needs to be checked against them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
The Rabbis (the חכמים)

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the challenge in step 4

steps.title: The רבנן contradict themselves
steps.stepSummary: If the תוספתא is the רבנן, its rice ruling (ברכה מעין שלש) clashes with the רבנן in the ברייתא, who said rice gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there is a contradiction between the רבנן and the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא the חכמים said "ולא כלום" for rice. The תוספתא, now attributed to the רבנן, gives rice a ברכה מעין שלש. Both cannot be the same רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The Rabbis contradict the Rabbis

phrases.english: If so,
there is a contradiction between the Rabbis and the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: Attributing the תוספתא to the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא's rice ruling conflicts with the רבנן's "ולא כלום" in the ברייתא

steps.title: Keep the רבנן and correct the rice line
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא really is the רבנן. Its rice line should be amended to read that after rice one says no blessing, meaning no ברכה מעין שלש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really it is the רבנן, and teach regarding rice: "and at the end he does not bless over it anything."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the problem by fixing the wording of the תוספתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crumbled-bread clause forces the תוספתא to be the רבנן. So the rice line is changed to match the רבנן in the ברייתא. Now the whole תוספתא is consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really
At the end, after eating

steps.whatToRemember: The תוספתא follows the רבנן. After rice there is no ברכה מעין שלש. In that תוספתא, bread whose pieces are no longer intact gets מזונות before and a ברכה מעין שלש after. Steps 20–21 give a different practical ruling for cooked bread crumbs.

phrases.english: Rather, actually it is the Rabbis,
and teach regarding rice:
'And at the end he does not recite any blessing over it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם רַבָּנַן, וּתְנִי גַּבֵּי אוֹרֶז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תוספתא gives rice a ברכה מעין שלש
steps.terutzMaskana: Rice gets no ברכה מעין שלש, in line with the רבנן

steps.title: רבא: the farmers' flour dish gets מזונות
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the farmers' ריהטא, which has a lot of flour, gets בורא מיני מזונות because the flour is the main part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this ריהטא of farmers, in which they put a lot of flour, one blesses בורא מיני מזונות. Why? Because the flour is the main ingredient.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts: which ברכה to say over a cooked dish of flour and honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא uses the rule of עיקר, the main ingredient. When flour is the majority, the dish takes the flour's ברכה, מזונות.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked dish of flour and honey
Farmers
Fine flour
The main ingredient

phrases.english: Rava said:
This flour-and-honey dish of the farmers
in which they add a lot of flour,
one blesses: 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment.'
What is the reason? Because the flour is the main part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Farmers' ריהטא, mostly flour, gets מזונות

steps.title: רבא: the מחוזא version gets שהכל
steps.stepSummary: The מחוזא version has less flour, so honey is the main part, and רבא first rules שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריהטא of מחוזא, where they do not add much flour, one blesses שהכל נהיה בדברו. Why? Because the honey is the main ingredient.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite ruling for the city recipe, which has less flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the same עיקר logic, the honey now dominates. So the dish follows the honey's ברכה, שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: מחוזא, a Babylonian city
Honey
The general blessing, שהכל

phrases.english: That of Mechoza, in which they do not add a lot of flour,
one blesses over it: 'By Whose word all things came to be.'
What is the reason? Because the honey is the main part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasting case to step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחוזא ריהטא, mostly honey, gets שהכל

steps.title: רבא changes his mind: both get מזונות
steps.stepSummary: רבא retracts and rules that both the farmers' and the מחוזא versions get בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא then said: both this and that get בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes back his split ruling. The next step gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא no longer measures which ingredient is bigger. Any real grain content gives the dish the grain's ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he retracted and said
Both this and that

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at steps 8–9. רבא's final ruling is that both versions get מזונות.

phrases.english: And Rava reconsidered and said:
Both this and that: 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retracts the ruling of step 9

steps.title: Source: רב and שמואל's five-grain rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא's retraction is based on רב and שמואל: anything containing one of the חמשת המינים gets בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב and שמואל both said: anything that has in it from the five species, one blesses over it בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רבא's new ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five grains are so important that even when they are not the majority, they set the ברכה. That is why the honey-heavy מחוזא dish is still מזונות.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
The five grains: wheat, barley, spelt, oats, rye

steps.whatToRemember: Any dish containing one of the five grains gets בורא מיני מזונות (רב and שמואל), even if another ingredient is the larger part.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic halachic rule for the ברכה over mixed foods containing grain.

phrases.english: As Rav and Shmuel both said:
Anything that contains any of the five species
one recites over it: 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 10
steps.raayaObject: רבא's final ruling that both versions get מזונות
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב and שמואל's rule about the five grains
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Five-grain content makes a dish מזונות

steps.title: רב יוסף's rule for a cooked dish with bread pieces
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that חביצא with כזית-sized bread pieces gets המוציא and ברכת המזון. Without כזית pieces, it gets בורא מיני מזונות and מעין שלש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This cooked dish (חביצא) that has bread pieces the size of a כזית: at the start one says המוציא, and at the end one says the three blessings of ברכת המזון. If it does not have pieces the size of a כזית: at the start one says בורא מיני מזונות, and at the end one says the one blessing that summarizes the three (מעין שלש).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. רב יוסף gives a ruling about a cooked dish made with bread pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size of the bread pieces decides everything. A piece the size of a כזית still counts as 'bread', so it gets the full bread ברכות. Smaller pieces lose their bread identity and are treated like a regular grain dish.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked dish containing bread pieces
Crumbs or pieces of bread
The size of an olive; a standard halachic measure
The three blessings of ברכת המזון
The one blessing that summarizes the three (על המחיה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule for when bread pieces cooked in a dish still count as bread. Practical halacha about cooked bread is built on this discussion.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי חֲבִיצָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ פֵּרוּרִין כְּזַיִת —
phrases.english: This cooked dish that has in it bread pieces the size of an olive —

phrases.aramaic: בַּתְּחִלָּה מְבָרֵךְ עָלָיו ״הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ״,
phrases.english: at the start one blesses over it 'Who brings forth bread from the earth,'
and at the end one recites over it three blessings (Grace after Meals).
One that does not have pieces the size of an olive —
at the start one blesses over it 'Who creates kinds of nourishment,'
and at the end one blessing summarizing the three.
phrases.notes: This is the ברכה of על המחיה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the ריהטא discussion (steps 8–11). Both topics deal with grain-based foods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread pieces of a כזית in a cooked dish keep bread status (המוציא and ברכת המזון). Smaller pieces get מזונות and מעין שלש.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from מנחות broken into כזית-sized pieces
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף proves his rule from a ברייתא. מנחות are broken into כזית pieces, yet one says המוציא over them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How do I know this? Because a ברייתא teaches: if someone was standing and offering מנחות in ירושלים, he says שהחיינו. When he takes them to eat them, he says המוציא. And another ברייתא teaches about this: all of them, he breaks them into pieces the size of a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a source to back up his ruling. Two ברייתות together show that כזית-sized pieces still get המוציא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says one makes המוציא over מנחות. The second ברייתא says מנחות are broken into כזית pieces. Put together, the proof is: כזית-sized pieces still count as bread for המוציא.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introducing a proof)
Flour-based offerings brought in the בית המקדש
The blessing for a new or first-time experience
He breaks them into pieces
And it was taught about it (a second ברייתא on the same topic)

steps.confusionAlert: The שהחיינו part is not the proof. The proof only comes from joining המוציא with the second ברייתא's 'פותתן כזית'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ — דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: From where do I say it? As it was taught:
If one was standing and offering meal-offerings in Jerusalem —
he says: 'Blessed… Who has given us life,
sustained us, and brought us to this time.'
When he took them to eat them —
he blesses 'Who brings forth bread from the earth.'
And it was taught about it: And all of them, he breaks them into olive-sized pieces.
phrases.notes: This line is the key to the proof. The pieces are only a כזית, yet they still get המוציא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's ruling in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's rule that כזית-sized bread pieces keep bread status
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתות about מנחות: one says המוציא over them, and they are broken into כזית pieces

steps.title: אביי asks: what about מנחות crushed back into flour?
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that by רב יוסף's logic, according to תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל (who crushes מנחות back into flour), no המוציא would be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, according to the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל, who says one crushes them until they become flour again, would it also be true that one does not need to say המוציא?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to attack רב יוסף's proof. He points to another opinion, where the מנחות are crushed into tiny crumbs, not כזית pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If crumb size really decides the ברכה, then under תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל the tiny crumbs would lose bread status and get no המוציא. אביי finds that result strange, and he sets up the next line to show it is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now… (pushing an idea to an odd result)
The Tanna of the school of רבי ישמעאל
He crushes them
Their fine flour (their original state)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But if so, now,
according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael
who said one crushes them until he returns them to their flour,
would it also be that one does not need to bless
'Who brings forth bread from the earth'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic behind רב יוסף's proof in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule that pieces smaller than a כזית lose bread status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, the מנחות are crumbs smaller than a כזית. By רב יוסף's rule they would get no המוציא, which seems hard to accept.

steps.title: אביי's proof that tiny crumbs still count as bread
steps.stepSummary: אביי blocks the answer 'yes, no המוציא'. A ברייתא says gathering a כזית from all the crumbs makes one liable for חמץ, or fulfills the מצוה of מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that is indeed so, but a ברייתא teaches: if one gathered a כזית from all of them and ate it, if it is חמץ he is punished with כרת, and if it is מצה a person fulfills his obligation with it on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes off an escape route for רב יוסף. He brings a ברייתא showing that tiny crumbs, put together to make a כזית, are still treated as real bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ and מצה both require real bread. So if crumbs gathered together count for כרת and for the מצוה of מצה, they have not lost their bread status. That suggests they should get המוציא too, which goes against רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say that it is indeed so
He gathered
Punishable by כרת (spiritual cutting off)
Fulfills his obligation

phrases.english: And if you say so indeed, but wasn't it taught:
If one gathered an olive-bulk from all of them and ate them,
if it is leavened — he is punishable by karet,
and if it is matza —

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם יוֹצֵא בּוֹ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: a person fulfills his obligation with it on Passover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's challenge from step 14 by bringing a source against the answer 'yes, no המוציא'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that crumbs smaller than a כזית are no longer bread
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא treats a כזית gathered from small crumbs as real bread for חמץ and מצה. So small crumbs keep bread status.

steps.title: The crumbs were pressed together into one mass
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about crumbs is talking about a case where they were stuck back together into one piece (שערסן).
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? Where he pressed them together (into one mass).
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given in defense of רב יוסף. The ברייתא about חמץ and מצה is limited to a special case where the crumbs were joined back together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the crumbs were kneaded or pressed into one mass, they form a real piece of bread again. So that ברייתא does not prove that loose small crumbs are bread, and רב יוסף's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (limiting a source to a specific case)
Where he pressed or kneaded them together into one mass

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where he compacted them together.
phrases.notes: The crumbs were joined into one mass, so they became a piece of bread again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that loose, tiny crumbs are still bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about crumbs that were pressed back into one mass.

steps.title: The plural wording 'he ate them' shows the crumbs were separate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer. The סיפא says 'שאכלן' (ate them, plural), but one joined mass would be 'שאכלו' (ate it).
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the ברייתא: 'provided he ate them within the time of eating a פרס.' But if he pressed them together, instead of 'he ate them' it should have said 'he ate it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 16 using the exact wording of the ברייתא. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'them' suggests separate crumbs eaten one by one over the time of כדי אכילת פרס. If they were pressed into one piece, the ברייתא would say 'it'. So the explanation שערסן seems not to fit the text.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Look at (say) the later clause
Within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf
It should have said

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
and that is when he ate them within the time of eating a half-loaf —
and if it is where he compacted them,
this 'that he ate them,'
it should have said 'that he ate it'?
phrases.notes: Singular would fit one joined mass. The plural points to separate crumbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer שערסן from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the crumbs were pressed together (שערסן)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's plural 'שאכלן' and the time limit of כדי אכילת פרס imply separate crumbs. One joined mass would be called 'שאכלו'.

steps.title: The crumbs came from a large loaf
steps.stepSummary: Replacing the rejected answer of 'stuck together,' the גמרא says the ברייתא's crumbs were broken off a large loaf of bread, so they still count as real bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with here? Crumbs that came from a large loaf of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous answer (the crumbs were stuck back together) was knocked down by the word 'שאכלן.' Now the גמרא gives a new answer: the crumbs were separate pieces, but they were broken off a big loaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crumbs broken off a real loaf were once full bread, so they keep bread status even when small and separate. That is different from the מנחה of תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, which was crushed all the way back into flour. So the ברייתא about crumbs no longer contradicts the idea that crushed מנחות lose their bread status.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the old answer and gives a new one)
What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower reading of a source)
Came from a large loaf of bread

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
With crumbs that came from a large loaf of bread.
phrases.notes: Each crumb was once part of a full loaf, so it keeps bread status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 17 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא): the ברייתא refers to crumbs from a large loaf.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The crumbs had to be stuck back into one piece to count, but that reading was disproved by 'שאכלן.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Separate crumbs count as bread because they came from a real loaf. This is unlike מנחות crushed back into flour.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: After all the proofs and rejections, the גמרא asks what the practical conclusion is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The back-and-forth has not settled anything, so the גמרא stops and asks for the bottom-line halacha. This line sets up רב ששת's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every proof for and against רב יוסף's rule was pushed aside. This question moves the discussion from debating sources to stating practical law.

keyTerms.meaning: What was concluded about it? (asks for the final halacha)

phrases.english: What was concluded about this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the debate and asks for the practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical halacha for bread pieces smaller than a כזית.

steps.title: A crumbled bread dish gets המוציא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that a cooked dish of bread crumbs (חביצא) gets המוציא, even if no piece is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Over this crumbled bread dish, even though it has no crumbs the size of a כזית, one says 'המוציא לחם מן הארץ.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. A dish made of bread crumbs gets the bread בְּרָכָה, even if every piece is smaller than a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes against רב יוסף's rule that the pieces must be a כזית to get המוציא. For רב ששת, being bread matters more than the size of the pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked dish made with bread crumbs
Crumbs
An olive's volume (a halachic size)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical halacha for cooked or crumbled bread dishes.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: This crumbled bread dish,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ פֵּרוּרִין כְּזַיִת —
phrases.english: even though it does not contain crumbs the size of an olive,
one recites over it: 'Who brings forth bread from the earth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A crumbled bread dish gets המוציא even without pieces the size of a כזית.

steps.title: Only if it still looks like bread
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits רב ששת's ruling: it applies only when the pieces still look like bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And this is only when it still has the look of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a condition to רב ששת's ruling. The crumbs get המוציא only if they have not dissolved and can still be seen as bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small size does not take away bread status, but losing the look of bread does. If the crumbs melt into mush, they no longer count as bread for המוציא.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when (introduces a condition)
The look or form of bread

steps.whatToRemember: Final halacha: bread crumbs in a cooked dish get המוציא even if they are smaller than a כזית, as long as they still look like bread (רב ששת and רבא).

phrases.english: Rava said:
And this is when it has on it the appearance of bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְהוּא דְּאִיכָּא עֲלֵיהּ תּוֹרִיתָא דְנַהְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to רב ששת's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המוציא applies to the crumbled dish only if the bread pieces still look like bread.

steps.title: טרוקנין require חלה
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens: one view says טרוקנין (an unusual baked item) must have חלה taken from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: טרוקנין are obligated in חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related question: does an unusually baked item count as bread? This first view says טרוקנין need חלה, so they count as bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only real bread dough needs חלה. Saying טרוקנין need חלה treats them as bread, which ties back to the theme of what counts as 'bread.'

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual baked item (defined below)
Obligated in separating חלה

phrases.english: Terokanin are obligated in challah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related topic about the status of bread.

steps.title: רבין reports: טרוקנין are exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings רבי יוחנן's opposite ruling from ארץ ישראל: טרוקנין are exempt from חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: טרוקנין are exempt from חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: A different tradition arrives from ארץ ישראל and rules the opposite way. According to רבי יוחנן, טרוקנין do not need חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two opposing views on the same item. The disagreement is whether this unusual way of baking makes the item real bread or not.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a teaching)
Exempt from חלה

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And when Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Terokanin are exempt from challah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite ruling from the view in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, טרוקנין are exempt from חלה.

steps.title: What are טרוקנין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what טרוקנין actually are.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are טרוקנין?
steps.whatsHappening: To understand the disagreement, the גמרא asks for a definition of the item. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether the item needs חלה depends on how it is made. So the גמרא first needs to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (asks for a definition)

phrases.english: What are terokanin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the item being debated.

steps.title: Baked in a hollow in the ground
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that טרוקנין are baked in a hollow dug in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is baked in a hollow in the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defines טרוקנין as something baked in a pit or hollow in the ground, not in a normal oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the baking method is unusual, it is unclear whether the item counts as real bread. That explains why one view requires חלה and רבי יוחנן exempts it.

keyTerms.meaning: A hollow or pit in the ground

phrases.english: Abaye said: A cavity in the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טרוקנין are baked in a hollow in the ground.

steps.title: טריתא is exempt from חלה
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that another unusual item, טריתא, is exempt from חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: טריתא is exempt from חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another ruling about an unusual 'bread': טריתא does not need חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the same theme. Some baked items are made so differently that they do not count as bread for חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of unusual baked item (defined below)

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
Terita is exempt from challah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טְרִיתָא פְּטוּרָה מִן הַחַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling on a similar unusual item.

steps.title: What is טריתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what טריתא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is טריתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of טריתא. This sets up three different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As before, we need to know how the item is made in order to understand why it is exempt from חלה.

phrases.english: What is terita?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the item in step 26.

steps.title: Three definitions of טריתא
steps.stepSummary: Three views: dough poured onto a boiling-hot surface, 'Indian bread,' or bread made for כותח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: kneaded dough on a boiling-hot surface. Some say: Indian bread. Some say: bread made for כותח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three opinions about what טריתא is. Each one is made in an unusual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each definition, the item is not normal bread. It is either cooked on a hot surface, baked in a special way, or made as an ingredient for a dip (כותח). That is why אביי exempts it from חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Kneaded dough poured onto a boiling-hot surface
Indian bread
A Babylonian dip or relish

steps.whatToRemember: Items made in very unusual ways (טרוקנין and טריתא) may lose bread status for חלה, just as bread crumbs keep bread status for המוציא only while they still look like bread.

phrases.english: Some say: kneaded dough on a boiling-hot surface;
and some say: bread of India;
and some say: bread made for kutach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 with three opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טריתא is either dough on a boiling-hot surface, Indian bread, or bread made for כותח.

steps.title: רבי חייא: Bread made for כותח is exempt from חלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that bread made to be eaten with כותח is exempt from חלה. This supports the view that טריתא is bread made for כותח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: Bread that is made for כותח is exempt from separating חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי חייא. It matches the last explanation of טריתא from the previous step, that טריתא is 'bread made for כותח', which אביי said is exempt from חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי ruled that טריתא is exempt from חלה, and one view said טריתא is bread made for כותח. רבי חייא's teaching says this exact thing: bread for כותח is exempt. So this ruling fits with, and backs up, that explanation of אביי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A sharp dip or relish (made with bread crumbs, whey and salt). People dipped bread into it.
Exempt from separating חלה (the portion of dough given to the כהן)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'bread made for כותח' is a known category that a ברייתא treats as exempt from חלה. That makes the third explanation of טריתא make sense.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught:
phrases.notes: This is an earlier teaching with real weight, brought to back up what was just said.

phrases.english: Bread that is made for kutach (a dip)
phrases.notes: The bread is made to be dipped into or eaten with כותח.

phrases.english: is exempt from challah.
phrases.notes: No need to separate חלה from this dough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the third view of what טריתא is (bread made for כותח), and supports אביי's ruling that it is exempt.
steps.raayaObject: That bread made for כותח (one explanation of טריתא) is exempt from חלה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says bread for כותח is obligated in חלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא with a ברייתא that says bread made for כותח IS obligated in חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא that it is obligated in חלה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two sources contradict each other. רבי חייא says bread for כותח is exempt, but another ברייתא says it is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources talk about the same item and give opposite rulings. If the ברייתא is right, the support for calling טריתא 'exempt' gets weaker. The גמרא now has to show how both sources can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? This phrase opens a challenge from an earlier source.
Obligated in חלה. One must separate חלה from it.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught (in a baraita):
phrases.notes: Standard way to start a challenge from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: it is obligated in challah!
phrases.notes: The exact opposite of רבי חייא's ruling about bread made for כותח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חייא's teaching with a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's ruling that bread made for כותח is exempt from חלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between two sources: one source says exempt, the other says obligated, about the same bread.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה: the way it is made shows its purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא that says 'obligated' gives its reason, the view of רבי יהודה. He says the way the bread is prepared shows what it is meant for, so not all bread for כותח is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, as the reason is taught in it: רבי יהודה says, 'Its actions prove what it is.' If he made them…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by looking at the reason the ברייתא itself gives. רבי יהודה says the way the bread was made tells us its purpose. This passage ends on 'If he made them', which sets up the details that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that says 'obligated' does not mean all bread for כותח needs חלה. It goes with רבי יהודה, who looks at how the bread was made. Some ways of making it show that it is real bread, so it is obligated. Other ways show it is only for the dip, so it is exempt. This way the two sources are talking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: There (pointing to the other source, the ברייתא)
As its reason is taught. The source explains itself.
Its actions (how it was made) prove what it is
He made them. This opens the case details that follow on the next amud.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two sources simply argue, with one saying 'always exempt' and the other 'always obligated'. The answer is that the ברייתא depends on HOW the bread was made. Some kinds of bread for כותח are obligated and some are exempt. The details continue right after 'עֲשָׂאָן'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general idea: whether something counts as 'bread' can depend on how it was prepared. Its form shows its purpose.

phrases.english: There (in that baraita), it is as its reason is taught —
phrases.notes: The ברייתא itself explains why it says 'obligated'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that says 'obligated' follows רבי יהודה's approach.

phrases.english: Its actions (the way it was made) prove what it is.
phrases.notes: The way the bread is prepared shows whether it is real bread or only for the dip.

phrases.english: If he made them
phrases.notes: This sentence continues on the next amud, which explains the different ways of making the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 30 by explaining the ברייתא through רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the ruling depends on how the bread is made, so the two sources talk about different kinds of bread.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources argue about all bread made for כותח.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה, the way the bread is made shows its purpose. Bread made like real bread is obligated, and bread made only for the dip is exempt. So the sources can both be right.
